fact: T-Rex had the strongest bite of any land animal ever — about 12,800 pounds of force! That's like having a small car dropped on you.
Velociraptors were actually only about the size of a turkey, not the giant creatures shown in movies!
The Argentinosaurus was so massive it weighed about 100 tons — that's heavier than 14 African elephants combined!
Stegosaurus had a brain the size of a walnut, but it had bony plates on its back that could flush with blood to regulate body temperature.
Pterodactyls weren't actually dinosaurs! They were flying reptiles called pterosaurs that lived alongside dinosaurs.
The name 'dinosaur' means 'terrible lizard' in Greek — but dinosaurs weren't actually lizards at all!
Spinosaurus is the largest known carnivorous dinosaur, even bigger than T-Rex! It was also a fantastic swimmer.
Triceratops' frill wasn't just for protection — scientists think it was used to attract mates, like a peacock's tail!
Some dinosaurs swallowed stones called gastroliths to help grind up food in their stomachs, kind of like how birds use grit today!
The Ankylosaurus had a tail club so powerful it could break the bones of a T-Rex. Talk about a built-in weapon!
Dinosaurs lived on every continent, including Antarctica! Back then, it was covered in forests, not ice.
The Micropachycephalosaurus has the longest name of any dinosaur — try saying that five times fast!
Birds are technically dinosaurs! They evolved from small theropod dinosaurs and are the only dinosaur lineage that survived the extinction.
Parasaurolophus had a long hollow crest on its head that it could use like a trumpet to make deep, booming sounds!
The asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs was about 6 miles wide — roughly the size of Mount Everest!
Brachiosaurus could eat leaves from trees up to 30 feet high — that's like eating off the roof of a three-story building!
Some dinosaur eggs were as big as footballs! The largest ever found belonged to a type of oviraptorosaur.
Compsognathus was one of the smallest dinosaurs — about the size of a chicken! But it was a fierce little predator.
The Utahraptor was the largest raptor dinosaur, about 23 feet long and 1,100 pounds. Now THAT's a raptor!
Dinosaurs dominated Earth for about 165 million years. Humans have only been around for about 300,000 years!
Pachycephalosaurus had a skull dome 10 inches thick! Scientists debate whether they head-butted each other like rams.
The Quetzalcoatlus had a wingspan of 36 feet — as wide as a small airplane! It was the largest flying animal ever.
Therizinosaurus had claws up to 3 feet long — the longest claws of any animal that ever lived!
The first dinosaur fossil ever scientifically described was Megalosaurus in 1824, by William Buckland in England.
Diplodocus could crack its tail like a whip, creating a sonic boom that could be heard from miles away!
Some scientists believe T-Rex had feathers — at least as a baby. Imagine a fluffy T-Rex chick!
Iguanodon was one of the first three dinosaurs ever named, and scientists originally put its thumb spike on its nose like a horn!
The Giganotosaurus from South America had a skull over 5 feet long — one of the biggest heads ever on a land predator!
Sauropod dinosaurs could grow so fast that some species gained up to 2 tons per year during their growth spurts!
Dreadnoughtus, meaning 'fears nothing', was one of the most massive land animals ever — weighing about 65 tons!
